Appearance & Visual Theme
Dark mode keeps the classic bevelled look using low-glare graphite tones optimized for live mixing booths.
Macro summary changes only how the WHEN / IF / THEN box is drawn: Lines is the classic three-line readout; Cards gives each part its own box, with the trigger facts, the gates and the numbered steps told apart. Neither changes what runs.
Workspace Layout
Use Re-centre windows if a dialog or one of the separate windows (Meter Bridge, Guide) was dragged off the edge of the screen: it puts them back in view. The editor is never closed by it.
Keeps master controls, transport buttons, status, and IP visible when scrolling vertically.
Live Operational Safety
Interactive Help & ScreenTips
Hovering over any control displays a classic tooltip detailing its function, live show impact, and engineering recommendation.
Warnings
The warnings you asked not to see again. Restoring one makes its dialog ask again the next time the action runs; the confirmations that destroy something are never listed, because they always ask.
Channel Matrix Selector
The matrix organizes channels into 8-fader banks matching the physical Behringer WING layout, enabling rapid block selection for mutes, faders, or alerts.
Matrix Quick Actions
Direct selection shortcuts available in the matrix toolbar:
  • 8-channel blocks: Select or toggle a whole block of the current family (CH 1-40, USB 1-48, ...).
  • Odd / Even: Select left or right channels for stereo pairs.
  • Invert: Invert active selection within the category.
Style, size, zoom, speed and peak hold below are the same settings as the Meters card in the main window: changing one moves the other immediately. There is no separate copy.

How to use this page (step by step)
MTC is the easy one: open our MIDI ports (previous page) and the position starts moving — no device and no permission needed.
LTC file (checked, not played): this build reads and reports an LTC file — the range it covers, whether it is drop-frame, which channel carried it — and it does not play one back, so a file never drives the show. Choose the file's own rate beside it (LTC does not carry one), then Verify an LTC file….
LTC from a device: press Refresh to ask the system what inputs exist, choose the device, the channel that carries timecode and the rate of the input — the rate of the incoming signal, which is a separate choice from the file's — then Listen. Changing that rate while the input is open reopens the stream at the new one. macOS asks for the microphone the first time, and an interface or a virtual audio device is what carries timecode in practice. If the interface is unplugged or another application takes it, the page says the stream stopped and Reconnect the input finds it again — and falls back to the system's default input when the device you chose is not listed any more. If nothing decodes for a few seconds, the status line names the rate in use and says that nothing arrived at it.
Make a cue: let the show run to the moment and press Add cue here, then choose the macro it fires. Building a long list is done with Add cue at the end, which appends after the last cue and leaves the list where it is. Its position can be edited on the row — hours, minutes, seconds and frames, with a nudge of ±1 or ±10 — and nothing is written until Save (re-arms), because saving re-arms every cue. A macro whose [!] Notice toggle is on shows its courtesy card when a cue fires it, exactly as it does for a trigger.
Offset: frames added to every source, for a feed that arrives a little late or early. It is saved with the cue list and applied before the cues are compared.
Watch it: Open the clock window for a second screen (large digits, a pin), or read the Timecode card in the right-hand column and the compact readout in the status area.
Pass it on: pass the timecode on as MTC sends what we are following out on our virtual MIDI port, with the offset applied.

The full chapter is chapter 13 of the guide — Timecode (MTC, LTC, SMPTE) — in Properties → Guide & Help.

How to use this page (step by step)
Nothing here runs until the switch above is on. With it off, no port exists, no socket is bound and no macro can be triggered from outside.

1. Switch it on, then add an application: for MIDI only the name matters; for OSC the address is also the listener's IP filter, so listing one restricts who the listener can hear. It limits who can talk to it; it does not authenticate anyone.
2. MIDI, in: open our ports, press Add a binding, press Learn, then press the control in the other application. Learn captures the message exactly as it arrives.
3. MIDI, out: a macro step of kind Send MIDI, or Send one message here to prove the path. PANIC STOP also sends All Sound Off and All Notes Off on all sixteen channels.
4. OSC, in: choose a port and where it may be reached from — this machine only is the default and the recommended one; the network is for a tablet or another laptop and is refused without at least one application listed, because filtering addresses is not authentication — then Start listening.
5. OSC, out: a macro step of kind Send OSC, with an address and typed arguments.
6. Conditions: a binding can ask something of the message before it fires, and a value that has gone stale never counts as met.

The full chapter is chapter 12 of the guide — MIDI and other applications — in Properties → Guide & Help.

Switching the feature off also stops whatever is running: the MIDI ports, the OSC listener, the audio input and anything being passed on. It is a switch, not a sign.

MIDI ports
Press Refresh to ask the system which MIDI ports exist. Listing them opens nothing.
Not open. Nothing is listened to.

Network (OSC)
Where it listens. This machine is the default and the recommended one; the network is for an application on another device (a tablet, another laptop); it is refused unless you have listed at least one application above, because on the network any device on that network can send an address that fires a macro. The list above is a filter of IP addresses: it limits who can be heard, it does not authenticate anyone — an address in a UDP packet can be forged.
Not listening.
Send one message (to set the other application up)
Nothing sent yet. This test sends the address with no arguments (arguments come with the macro step), so it is right for a start/stop style address and not yet for setting a value.
Each trigger fires one macro, with the same guards, Stop button and overlap rules as a macro fired by hand.
This is the first step: the switch and the list. MIDI comes next (so a macro can press a button in Mixing Station and a button there can fire a macro), and OSC after that. See docs/INTER_APP_PLAN_REVIEW_2026-10-02.md.

Fallback: when the Meter Bridge is closed, alerts are always shown on the Main Station. This cannot be turned off, so it is a note, not a control.

Courtesy Trigger Notices

Non-intrusive floating toast notifications confirming macro execution in the screen corner without disrupting the live view.

The flash pulses the card's outline once a second — deliberately below the three-per-second rate that makes a flashing surface unsafe — and it is switched off entirely when the system asks for reduced motion. The accent colour applies to ordinary notices only: a failed action keeps its red caption and a test keeps its blue one, because those two colours are what the card is saying.

Toggle individual notices per-macro in Block 1 or the [!] Notice button in Saved Macros.
Eleven chapters: triggers, actions and their timing, macros and limits, meters and banks, saving and scopes, the WING protocol, diagnostics, troubleshooting, shortcuts, and recipes for real shows. With search and print, in its own window.
What this is, in three lines
· It watches the console (live meters and console state) and fires OSC commands when a value you defined crosses a threshold.
· A macro is WHEN (trigger) + optional IF gates + THEN (an ordered list of actions). Nothing runs until the macro is ENABLED and a session is live.
· It is not a remote or an editor: you mix on the console, this app reacts.
Start in two steps
1. Type the console IP in the Connection card (or use Discover WING in Properties → Console & Network).
2. Press Connect + Listen. The status chip turns Live and the meters start moving.
Safety, in three rules
· Arming is for testing and is never saved; ENABLED is what runs in a show. Both are needed.
· PANIC STOP (F12) aborts the app's pending commands and stops the stream. It cannot undo what the console already applied. With a broadcast alert on screen the header stays clickable above it and the alert card has its own PANIC STOP.
· Live Safe Mode blocks library changes, arming and test sends while a session runs; the chip says [LOCKED] when it is on.
What is where
· Connection: console IP, connect/disconnect, panic, and the session summary.
· Build Macro: trigger, IF gates, action timeline, preflight and Test Action (Shoot).
· Live Meters: the watchlist, the bank selector and the meters; Only meters hides the controls.
· Diagnostics: health grid, OSC monitor, log and probes — the first place to look when something is wrong.
· Session Log: the bounded event history of this session.
